source_snapshot.procedure: Copied three-option Set Power Restore Policy workflow using Chassis 00h/06h, BMC cold reset and physical AC removal/restoration.
source_snapshot.criteria: Copied restore-policy bits and post-AC behavior, not power-cycle off-duration timing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes unsubstantiated Chassis 00h/2Ch with a millisecond value and 00h/2Dh read.

old_problem: The historical review correctly identified the copied Power Restore Policy procedure and rejected DeepSeek's invented 2Ch/2Dh commands, but it missed the standard IPMI Set Power Cycle Interval command. IPMI 2.0 defines Chassis 00h/Cmd 0Bh, one interval byte in seconds and non-volatile behavior. It does not define a Get command, so completion alone is insufficient and the setting must be proven by an approved power-cycle timing observation and restored from a Project-authoritative baseline.
disposition_reason: Replace the copied policy workflow only in the review layer with standard Chassis 00h/0Bh and one 00h-FFh interval byte. Reject both the source's 00h/06h policy commands and DeepSeek's unsupported 2Ch/2Dh millisecond interpretation. Because the standard has no interval readback, validate a configured value only through one separately authorized Chassis Control power cycle while independent telemetry measures main-system OFF-to-ON duration; then require complete OFF to ON to OS Ready evidence. Restore a known Project baseline and functionally verify that restoration with its own authorized cycle or an independently approved authoritative readback. Missing baseline, measurement tolerance, maintenance approval or recovery leaves execution NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending. No power action is performed by this review.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1057-1059 and 1063, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code is unique. Related OOB row 1185 / Wistron-BMC-00475-V003 / variant 009288d6d9cc9d42 was directly read and remains distinct. Formal queue sequence 67 was independently verified as row 1063 / variant bd59d5d7ad14f965.

IPMI v2.0 section 28.9 and Appendix G assign Set Power Cycle Interval to Chassis NetFn 00h, command 0Bh. Request data is exactly one byte: 00h means no delay and nonzero values are 1-based seconds. The setting is non-volatile.

The interval applies to the time main system power remains down during a power-cycle action initiated by Chassis Control or a watchdog. It is not AC-removal dwell, BMC reset duration, request-to-OS-ready time or power-restore policy.

IPMI 2.0 defines no Get Power Cycle Interval companion command. Therefore completion 00h establishes request acceptance only; functional off-duration telemetry is required to prove the active setting, and a known approved baseline is required for deterministic restore.

The source body and Criteria are an exact semantic copy of adjacent Set Power Restore Policy row 1057. Running 00h/06h, BMC cold reset or AC unplug/replug would test another case and cannot satisfy interval coverage.
DeepSeek's 00h/2Ch, 00h/2Dh and millisecond unit conflict with the standard command assignment and are rejected; no OEM command is substituted without separate authority.

A power-cycle stimulus is service-affecting. It must start from a quiesced ON system, use independent main-power telemetry, prove complete OFF to ON to OS Ready, and have owner-approved interval/tolerance, workload safety and recovery. These are bounded Project runtime parameters under ED-18, not an unresolved standard semantic.

A no-delay or nonzero target does not define an acceptable measurement tolerance. Per ED-15, the Project must approve the fixture resolution and numeric acceptance window before any PASS; missing threshold is NOT READY.

ED-06 keeps power-cycle semantics distinct from BMC cold reset and AC/DC cycles; ED-14 prohibits replacing a formal interval test with a short smoke; ED-17 preserves logs; ED-18 requires OFF to ON to OS Ready; ED-19 keeps IB and OOB identities separate; ED-28/ED-30 require safe recovery; ED-38 prohibits automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set Power Cycle Interval (IB Chassis 00h/0Bh) measured OFF interval and restore
test_case.purpose: Set an approved non-volatile power-cycle off interval over the local system interface, prove its effect with independent main-power timing during a complete authorized power cycle, and restore and re-verify the Project baseline without conflating power-restore policy, BMC reset, AC cycling or the OOB variant.
required_package: Approved SUT/chassis/BMC/firmware and local IPMI system interface, verified support for optional Chassis 00h/0Bh, independent OOB console and authorized maintenance owner

Project-authoritative BASE_INTERVAL_SECONDS and approved TARGET_INTERVAL_SECONDS matrix in 0-255, with 00 explicitly interpreted as no intentional delay; numeric acceptance windows and fixture resolution for each value

Quiesced-data/workload plan, pre-cycle power-ON and sleep-state check, OS-ready oracle, maximum recovery time and independent main-system power-rail telemetry that distinguishes host OFF/ON from BMC standby power

Versioned in-band runner restricted to Chassis 00h/0Bh [one byte] plus separately gated Chassis Control 00h/02h [02h] stimulus, monotonic timestamp correlation, exact baseline restore and zero automatic retries
Preserved SEL/system/audit logs, immediate confirmation before each setter and each power cycle, pre-staged OOB/physical recovery and an authorized engineer to issue per-value and overall verdicts
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED SERVICE-AFFECTING PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve logs; do not run the copied 00h/06h policy, BMC-reset or AC-unplug steps and reject 00h/2Ch/2Dh. Verify exact chassis/BMC/firmware, authoritative BASE_INTERVAL_SECONDS, setter support, independent telemetry, recovery and numeric tolerance. With the host ON, below S4/S5, quiesced and OS-ready, for each separately approved target process one value before the next: encode seconds as one byte, display value/tolerance/service impact for immediate approval, send exactly once over `-I open` Chassis 00h/0Bh [TARGET], and require completion 00h without calling it PASS. Obtain a second immediate approval, start synchronized main-power/OOB/OS/log capture, then send exactly one Chassis Control 00h/02h [02h]. Require observable main host power OFF, measure OFF-edge to ON-edge against the approved target window, and require full ON to OS Ready plus healthy OOB/log/data state. Before another target, send BASE through 00h/0Bh once and functionally verify the baseline with one separately approved cycle; an authoritative Project/OEM readback may replace that restore cycle only when its command and equivalence are independently approved. Stop after any mismatch. Never infer a baseline, measure request-to-OS-ready as the interval, use AC/DC interruption, issue a cold reset, retry or continue without a verified restore.
test_case.expected_result: Each approved 00h/0Bh write returns completion 00h. Its single approved Chassis Control power cycle transitions through main-system OFF and ON; independent telemetry measures the OFF duration inside the pre-approved numeric window for TARGET seconds, after which the system reaches the defined OS Ready state with OOB access, data and preserved logs healthy. The exact baseline setter and separate restore evidence produce the baseline timing window and complete OFF to ON to OS Ready behavior. Unsupported command, missing OFF edge, measured interval outside the threshold, host previously off, power-up without a true cycle, incomplete OS recovery, collateral reset/AC behavior or unverified baseline restoration is FAIL/NOT READY without retry. Completion alone cannot pass.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires the exact Source Key/variant, Chassis 00h/0Bh with one seconds byte, an authoritative known baseline, approved numeric timing window, independent main-power edges, one authorized complete OFF to ON to OS Ready cycle for the target, exact restore and functional or independently authoritative restore verification. The copied 00h/06h policy workflow, DeepSeek 2Ch/2Dh milliseconds, command success alone, BMC reset, AC/DC unplug, elapsed time to OS Ready substituted for off duration, smoke-only observation, missing threshold, OOB evidence substituted for this IB setter, automatic retry or incomplete restore cannot pass. N/A requires authoritative platform evidence that optional 00h/0Bh is unsupported.
safety_gate: Use only the local system interface for this IB setter identity. OOB is an observer/recovery channel; row 1185 remains separately reviewable coverage.
Require a declared baseline before any write and pre-stage its exact one-byte restore through an independent path. No known baseline means NOT READY.
Before each power cycle, require quiesced storage/workload, host currently ON and below S4/S5, stable OOB/telemetry, OS-ready oracle, maximum recovery timeout and immediate maintenance approval.
Measure host main-power OFF-to-ON edges. Do not remove AC/DC input, reset the BMC, treat BMC standby continuity as host ON, or conflate reboot duration with the configured interval.
Preserve SEL/system/audit evidence and stop after the first abnormal edge, timeout, data/log error or restore mismatch. Do not clear logs or launch another target.
No automatic retry. If the host fails to return, the authorized owner uses the pre-approved OOB/physical recovery; the agent does not issue another cycle, reset, AC action or guessed interval.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; chassis/BMC/firmware/local-interface identity; official 00h/0Bh authority; distinct row-1185 OOB identity and no copied policy coverage credited
Authoritative baseline, per-target one-byte seconds value, numeric acceptance window, telemetry resolution, maintenance approvals and versioned runner hash
Redacted 00h/0Bh request/completion plus synchronized monotonic command, main-power OFF edge, main-power ON edge, measured duration, OOB console and OS-ready timestamps
Complete OFF to ON to OS Ready evidence, preserved SEL/system logs, data/workload health and proof no AC/DC or BMC-reset action occurred
Exact baseline restore command and independent baseline functional timing or separately approved authoritative readback evidence
Per-target PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A table and engineer verdict, explicitly recording that the review agent executed no DUT or power action
test_case.recovery: Before setting TARGET, pre-stage Chassis 00h/0Bh [BASE] for the local and owner-approved independent recovery paths. If target write acceptance is ambiguous, perform no power cycle and restore BASE once if safe. If the cycle starts but OFF/ON/OS Ready or timing is abnormal, stop all automation, preserve telemetry/console/logs and let the maintenance owner recover through the documented OOB/physical path; do not cycle again. Once stable, restore BASE exactly once and require a separately authorized baseline verification cycle or approved authoritative readback before closure. Never cold-reset the BMC, remove AC/DC, clear logs or retry automatically.

source_conflict.reason: Official section 28.9 resolves the title/body/DeepSeek conflict: the review layer uses Chassis 00h/0Bh seconds and functional timing, excludes copied 00h/06h policy/AC/BMC-reset steps and rejects unsupported 2Ch/2Dh without editing Master history.

blocked.reason: Core command, unit, range, persistence, functional stimulus and oracle are standardized. Baseline, chosen values, measurement tolerance, fixture and service/recovery approvals are finite Project execution prerequisites.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Section 28.9/Table 28-10 and Appendix G define Chassis 00h/Cmd0Bh, its one-byte 0-255 seconds encoding, 00h no-delay meaning, non-volatile behavior and application to Chassis Control/watchdog power-cycle off duration; section 28.3 supplies the guarded power-cycle stimulus semantics.

project_authority: Platform owners provide the exact supported firmware, known baseline, target values, numerical tolerance and measurement fixture; authorize each setter and service-affecting cycle; define OS Ready and recovery; and issue verdicts. They may mark the optional command N/A only from authoritative platform evidence. They cannot approve the copied policy workflow, unverified 2Ch/2Dh, milliseconds, completion-only PASS, missing threshold/baseline, AC/BMC reset substitution, automatic retry or incomplete recovery.
